The J29 Toyota Supra and G29 BMW Z4 Are Officially Sold Out in the US Market
27 photos
Photo: BMW
Internally referred to as J29 and G29, the current generations of the Supra and Z4 have finally disappeared from US new car inventories. Magna Steyr, the contract manufacturer that used to make them, wrapped up the program back in March 2026. Dealers nationwide have exhausted remaining stock, marking the end of an era for both Toyota and BMW.
CarsDirect reported on this first, with CarsDirect also highlighting that both companies prepared for the bitter end as early as April 2025. That's when Toyota introduced the Final Edition of the GR Supra, with BMW following suit in December 2025.
Considering that two-door sports cars are hard to sell nowadays, their US-market figures leave much to be desired. Throughout 2025, the rear-drive models racked up a pitiful 5,066 deliveries. To understand how bad that figure is, the aging ND Miata sold 8,727 units.
In the first nine months of 2026, the Supra and Z4 clocked 2,437 and 1,983 deliveries, respectively. Given the aforementioned, the ND-generation Miata will once again outsell them. Per Mazda's September 2026 report, both the canvas-topped model and the RF totaled 7,598 deliveries in the first three quarters.
All in all, it's a disappointing end for two models that would not have been possible had BMW and Toyota not agreed to join forces. The J29-generation Supra gave the Japanese automaker a compact rear-drive coupe with a turbo'd inline-six, while BMW stuck to the Z4's traditional formula.
Photo: Toyota Developing a dedicated sports car platform independently would have been a poor financial decision, as evidenced by the most recent sales volumes in the US market. Sharing the engineering, meanwhile, gave both parties a way to keep these relatively low-volume models commercially viable.
BMW debuted the Z4 first, with the G29 making its first public appearance in August 2018 at the Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance. 2019 was the first model year in the United States of America. The GR Supra, meanwhile, went live at the 2019 North American International Auto Show in Detroit. As such, the fixed-head J29 went on sale for the 2020 model year.
Both models offered inline-four options, and both also featured manual options. The manual for the inline-six lump had to wait a little, and truth be told, I wouldn't have either model in any other way. Think about it for a minute. Who in the world is okay with ponying up a lot of money for a four-pot manual Z4 when the MX-5 offers a more organic experience at a lower price?
Toyota was the first to join the BMW-sourced I6 engine with a manual, with BMW following suit. The German partner called the Z4 M40i with said tranny Handschalter, which is German for hand shifter.
The Z4 and Supra are both gone from their respective online configurators, and the Z4 won't return anytime soon. Over at 'Yota, the sixth-generation Supra is moving away from BMW to become an in-house Gazoo Racing project. To be revealed by the end of the decade, the newcomer should feature a new 2.0-liter turbo inline-four capable of more than 400 ponies.
